title: Algorithms and Coding
intro: Algorithms, bugs, loops and how computers follow instructions.

options.label: A set of step-by-step instructions to solve a problem

questions.explanation: An algorithm is a list of steps, in the right order, for completing a task or solving a problem.

questions.prompt: What do we call a mistake in a computer program?
questions.explanation: A mistake in a program is called a bug.

questions.prompt: What is it called when you find and fix mistakes in a program?
questions.explanation: Debugging means finding and fixing the bugs in a program so it works properly.

questions.prompt: What do we call a part of a program that repeats instructions?
questions.explanation: A loop repeats instructions, which saves writing the same steps again and again.

questions.prompt: Carrying out instructions one after another, in order, is called…
questions.explanation: Sequence means following steps in the right order. Getting the order wrong can change the result.

questions.prompt: Using "if" to choose what a program does next is called…
questions.explanation: Selection lets a program make a choice: if something is true, do one thing; otherwise do another.

questions.prompt: A computer can only follow the instructions it has been given.
questions.explanation: Computers do exactly what their programs tell them, which is why clear, correct algorithms matter.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a block-based programming language often used in schools?
questions.explanation: Scratch lets you snap together coding blocks to make animations, stories and games.

questions.prompt: In an algorithm, the order of the steps never matters.
questions.explanation: The order matters. Putting on your shoes before your socks would not work!
